title: Roll a TripleFlask flat from a lean so its layers match
instruction: Spread the medium in the TripleFlask evenly over its three layers, then leave the flask lying flat in its growth position, imprint up, with both hands off it.
context: Why: multilayer flasks are how research and biomanufacturing labs grow adherent cells past single-flask scale, and each seeding must leave the same volume of suspension on every layer: a layer that gets less grows sparse, one that gets more wastes medium and cells, and the whole flask is harvested at once. The knack: the three compartments share medium through the flask's closed end, so it keeps running down into the lower layers for as long as the flask is being turned flat. The maker's technical note says to stand the flask on end so the compartments level (where this task starts), rest it on its side, hold it at 75 degrees to the work surface, then quickly but gently tilt it into the growth position, imprint up. Tipped straight over from standing at a careful pace, or rolled slowly, the bottom layer ends too full; landed hard, medium splashes into the neck. Done by: cell-culture technicians and research associates in academic and biotech labs.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table top. Work surface: the station table, an open lab bench (the medium is dyed water, so no biosafety cabinet is used). Flask: a Thermo Scientific Nunc TripleFlask, Nunclon Delta treated, straight neck, with its solid (non-vented) screw cap, cat. 132867 (about 11 US dollars each in a case of 32), clear polystyrene plastic with an HDPE plastic cap: a 205 mm long body, 147 mm wide and 56 mm thick (the T175 size), with a 30 mm neck 20 mm long and a 40 mm cap 25 mm long, centred on the neck end. Inside are three culture compartments, each 170 x 98 mm with a 13 mm gap, at a 15 mm pitch (500 cm2 in all); they are joined at the closed end by a slot above 7 mm lips, and at the neck end each opens over a 7 mm lip into the neck chamber, whose 28 mm bore leads to the cap. 0.25 kg empty (estimate), 0.45 kg filled. The Nunclon imprint is on the top face. Medium: 200 mL of tap water tinted with 10 drops of McCormick blue food colour and 1 drop of dish soap (it flattens the meniscus for the photo reading), in place of a cell suspension. Start: the flask has been filled and capped tight, and stands upright on its closed end, cap up, so the compartments level (the maker's first step). Its long axis is vertical, the closed end flat on the table; the body's width runs along y from 13.75 to 28.45 cm, the top face toward the robot at x 13.4 cm and the bottom face at x 19 cm; the cap's centre is at x 16.2, y 21.1 cm, 23.75 cm up. Each compartment holds 66.7 mL, about 52.3 mm deep at the closed end. Laid on its long side about the closed end's edge at y 13.75 cm, it lies with the cap toward the robot's right (cap centre at y -10 cm, 7.35 cm up) and each compartment's 66.7 mL stands 30.2 mm deep. Surfaces: friction 0.35 between the flask and the work surface and between the flask and the gripper pads (estimate). Both arms start in their ready pose. One fixed layout, zero object jitter. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged at the end from photos and video. Layer volumes: the table is levelled to 0.2 degrees (phone inclinometer) before the trial; the flask is read flat where it lies. A phone on a lab jack 30 cm from a long side, raised to each layer's surface in turn (edge-on), photographs that layer beside a printed millimetre scale taped to the wall. In each photo the blue band's height (its floor to the flat surface just below the meniscus line) is measured at 3 marked points, at 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 of the length; then the same on the other long side, and the 6 are averaged (reading error about 0.1 mm, 2.5%). Only the phone's height changes, so wall offset and perspective scale the three layers alike: each layer's average is compared with the three layers' mean, an even split since all 200 mL stays in the layers. Each floor is 170 x 98 mm (166.6 cm2), so an even 66.7 mL stands 4.0 mm deep. In the sim: the medium model's three volumes. Even: every layer within 10% of the mean (3.6-4.4 mm when the mean reads 4.0; 60.0-73.3 mL). Roughly even: within 25% (3.0-5.0 mm; 50.0-83.3 mL). Flat: lying on its bottom face, imprint up, the top face within 5 degrees of level (inclinometer), resting on the table. Released and still: no gripper within 2 cm of the flask, and no point of it moving more than 1 mm over the last 3 s (video; a returning hand restarts the count). Score 0 if, at any time, even if it drains back: medium reaches the neck (more than 0.5 mL in the neck chamber; real: a pool of blue there, 0.5 mL lying about 0.8 mm deep over the 28 mm bore, in a neck photo before the cap is opened; a wet film from the dried refill does not count), any corner or the cap reaches the table faster than 0.5 m/s (a splash over the lips, 0 even if the neck stays dry; a 120 fps slow-motion video from 50 cm, level with the table, a 1 cm grid card behind: over 4 mm per frame in the last 4 frames before contact), or the flask leaves the table (any point 1 cm below the table top). Otherwise, at the end, the first that fits: 1.0 flat, released and still, every layer even; 0.5 flat, released and still, every layer roughly even; 0.25 flat, released and still, some layer outside 3.0-5.0 mm (50.0-83.3 mL); 0 anything else, including the untouched start (standing on end), the flask imprint down, on its side or on end, still held or not still. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. The trial ends at the run limit or once 1.0 has held; only the end counts, except the zeros above.
run_limit: 1,500 steps (75 s at 20 Hz); the scripted two-hand demo reaches full score in about 34 s
reset_notes: Nothing is used up. After the layers are read, pour the 200 mL out through the neck, then back in, dry the neck chamber and cap thread with a twist of paper towel and cap it tight; stand the flask upright on its closed end, cap up, on the start marks (top face toward the robot, the body's right edge at y 13.75 cm) and wait 10 s so the compartments level; check with the level that it stands upright. Replace the flask if dye stains the neck. Run the simulator with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Rigid flask at real size, 0.45 kg with medium, mass spread by volume, drawn clear (edges, shelves); cap and neck as 16 flats. The medium is an analytic model, not drawn: three compartment volumes whose levels follow the flask's pose, joined at the closed end by a slot (2.5 mL/s per mm of level gap), kept apart flat by 7 mm lips. Medium over a neck-end lip, or a corner landing faster than 0.5 m/s, goes to the neck. Slot rate, lips and landing limit are estimates. Nothing is moved by code.
